name: Tomato Pappu
subtitle: andhra everyday toor dal cooked soft with sour tomato and garlic

ingredients.note: Andhra pappu is meant to be hot
only if the tomatoes are not sour enough
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Rinse the toor dal until the water runs clear, which stops the dal frothing over.
Chop the tomatoes coarsely; they go into the cooker with the dal and melt away.
Crush the garlic with the flat of a knife rather than mincing it — you want soft sweet cloves at the end.

steps.text: Pressure cook the dal with the tomatoes, green chilli, turmeric and 2.5 cups water for 5 whistles.
steps.tip: Cooking the tomato with the dal, not after, is what makes it pappu rather than dal with tomato.

steps.text: Let the pressure drop naturally, open, and mash the dal against the side of the pot until smooth.
Add the salt, chilli powder and tamarind if using, with 1/2 cup water, and simmer 5 minutes.
Adjust with hot water until it pours thickly off the ladle.
Heat the oil in a small pan and pop the mustard seeds, then add the cumin.
Add the crushed garlic and fry until the cloves turn golden at the edges, about 1 minute.
steps.tip: Garlic browned properly here is most of the flavour; pale garlic tastes raw in the dal.

steps.text: Add the onion and fry 3 minutes until soft and lightly browned.
Add the red chilli, curry leaves and hing and let them crackle for 15 seconds.
Pour the tempering into the dal, stir once, scatter the coriander and serve over hot rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens as it stands. Reheat with a splash of water and a fresh squeeze of lemon if it tastes tired.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
